10.1016/j.cell.2025.04.001: Leptin acts in the brain to suppress appetite, yet the responsible neurocircuitries underlying leptin's anorectic effect are incompletely defined. Prepronociceptin (PNOC)-expressing neurons mediate diet-induced hyperphagia and weight gain in mice. Here, we show that leptin regulates appetite and body weight via PNOC neurons, and that loss of leptin receptor (Lepr) expression in PNOC-expressing neurons in the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus (ARC) causes hyperphagia and obesity. Restoring Lepr expression in PNOC neurons on a Lepr-null obese background substantially reduces body weight. Lepr inactivation in PNOC neurons increases neuropeptide Y (Npy) expression in a subset of hypothalamic PNOC neurons that do not express agouti-related peptide (Agrp). Selective chemogenetic activation of PNOC/NPY neurons promotes feeding to the same extent as activating all PNOCARC neurons, and overexpression of Npy in PNOCARC neurons promotes hyperphagia and obesity. Thus, we introduce PNOC/NPYARC neurons as an additional critical mediator of leptin action and as a promising target for obesity therapeutics.
10.1016/j.cell.2025.06.008: Virtual cells are an emerging frontier at the intersection of artificial intelligence and biology. A key goal of these cell state models is predicting cellular responses to perturbations. The Virtual Cell Challenge is being established to catalyze progress toward this goal. This recurring and open benchmark competition from the Arc Institute will provide an evaluation framework, purpose-built datasets, and a venue for accelerating model development.
10.1016/j.cmet.2024.12.001: De novo lipogenesis (DNL) is the process whereby cells synthesize fatty acids from acetyl-CoA, contributing to steatosis in fatty liver disease. Two new studies, using genetic mouse models, metabolomics, and pharmacology, identified alternative pathways in DNL and unexpected physiological effects when targeting key enzymes in this pathway.
10.1016/j.tem.2024.12.008: Recent advances in lineage-tracing technologies have significantly improved our understanding of pancreatic cell biology, particularly in elucidating the ontogeny and regenerative capacity of pancreatic cells. A deeper appreciation of the mechanisms underlying pancreatic cell identity and plasticity holds the potential to inform the development of new therapeutic modalities for conditions such as diabetes and pancreatitis. With this goal in mind, here we summarize advances, challenges, and future directions in tracing pancreatic cell origins and fates using lineage-tracing technologies. Given their essential role for blood glucose regulation, we pay particular attention on the insights gained from endocrine cells, especially β-cells.
10.1016/j.tem.2025.01.003: Mitochondria perform essential metabolic processes that sustain cellular bioenergetics and biosynthesis. In a recent article, Ryu et al. explored how mitochondria coordinate biochemical reactions with opposing redox demands within the same cell. They demonstrate that subcellular mitochondrial heterogeneity enables metabolic compartmentalization to permit concurrent oxidative ATP production and reductive proline biosynthesis.
10.1016/j.tig.2024.11.005: The increasing prevalence of genome sequencing and assembly has uncovered evidence of hyperdivergent genomic regions - loci with excess genetic diversity - in species across the tree of life. Hyperdivergent regions are often enriched for genes that mediate environmental responses, such as immunity, parasitism, and sensory perception. Especially in self-fertilizing species where the majority of the genome is homozygous, the existence of hyperdivergent regions might imply the historical action of evolutionary forces such as introgression and/or balancing selection. We anticipate that the application of new sequencing technologies, broader taxonomic sampling, and evolutionary modeling of hyperdivergent regions will provide insights into the mechanisms that generate and maintain genetic diversity within and between species.
10.1038/s43587-024-00802-0: We conducted a pace-of-aging analysis to evaluate healthspan and lifespan outcomes. Using longitudinal biomarker data and multi-omics profiling, we identified key aging trajectories associated with differential healthspan outcomes. Our findings demonstrate that the pace of biological aging, as measured by composite biomarker panels, is a strong predictor of both healthspan duration and overall lifespan, with implications for personalized anti-aging interventions.
10.1038/s41558-025-02301-5: This review examines the latest evidence on climate change mitigation strategies, focusing on adaptation frameworks and their effectiveness across diverse geographic regions. We synthesize findings from recent modeling studies, observational data, and policy analyses to assess the feasibility of achieving Paris Agreement targets. Our analysis highlights the gap between current policy trajectories and required emission reduction pathways.
10.1038/s41560-024-01696-3: We present an improved methodology for calculating energy return on investment (EROI) across hydrogen production pathways. Our framework addresses inconsistencies in existing EROI calculations by incorporating system boundary standardization, temporal dynamics, and infrastructure lifecycle impacts. Results show that green hydrogen via electrolysis achieves EROI values of 8-12 under optimized conditions, while blue hydrogen pathways exhibit greater variability depending on carbon capture rates.
10.48550/arXiv.2604.18584: We introduce MathNet, a global multimodal benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning and retrieval capabilities in AI systems. The benchmark spans 15 mathematical domains across 6 difficulty levels and includes both visual and textual problem representations. Evaluation of state-of-the-art models reveals significant performance gaps in multi-step reasoning and cross-modal mathematical understanding.
10.48550/arXiv.2604.18547: We propose FUSE, a framework for ensembling verification methods using zero labeled data. 10.48550/arXiv.2604.18566: We benchmark system dynamics AI assistants on causal loop diagram (CLD) extraction tasks, comparing cloud-based and locally-deployed large language models. Our evaluation framework assesses causal structure identification, feedback loop detection, and dynamic hypothesis generation across 50 system dynamics models. Results show that cloud models outperform local models by 23% on complex multi-loop systems while local models achieve competitive performance on simpler structures.
10.1056/AIoa2400859: We developed TRIALSCOPE, a simulation framework for clinical trials using real-world data. The platform integrates electronic health records, claims data, and patient registries to generate synthetic control arms and predict trial outcomes. Validation against 12 completed randomized controlled trials demonstrates that TRIALSCOPE achieves predictive accuracy within 5% of actual trial results for primary endpoints, enabling more efficient trial design and patient stratification.
10.1056/NEJMe2412176: This editorial discusses recent milestones in gene-editing therapies, highlighting the approval of CRISPR-based treatments for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia. We examine the clinical evidence supporting these approvals, discuss manufacturing and delivery challenges, and consider the broader implications for genetic medicine. The field is poised for rapid expansion as next-generation editing platforms address current limitations in specificity and delivery.
10.1056/EVIDe2500054: This review examines the epidemiology of obesity, noting that prevalence has reached 40% in many populations and continues to rise. We analyze contributing factors including dietary patterns, sedentary behavior, genetic predisposition, and environmental influences. The review synthesizes evidence on pharmacological interventions, particularly GLP-1 receptor agonists, and their role in managing the obesity epidemic at population scale.
10.48550/arXiv.2604.18570: We present Apollo, a multimodal temporal foundation model designed for virtual patient representation at healthcare system scale. Apollo integrates longitudinal clinical data, imaging, and genomic information through a unified temporal architecture. Evaluated across three hospital systems with over 500,000 patient records, Apollo demonstrates superior performance in clinical prediction tasks including 30-day readmission, disease progression modeling, and treatment response prediction.
10.48550/arXiv.2604.18541: We introduce CoVeR, a contrastive verification framework for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems. CoVeR learns to verify retrieved passages against generated claims through contrastive training on synthetically generated verification pairs. Our approach improves factual accuracy by 15-22% on knowledge-intensive QA benchmarks while maintaining computational efficiency through lightweight verification heads.
10.1016/S0140-6736(25)00678-6: This health economics evaluation examines the cost-effectiveness of preventive healthcare interventions across multiple chronic disease categories. Using lifetime microsimulation modeling, we estimate that population-level screening programs for cardiovascular disease, diabetes, and cancer yield net savings of $2,400-4,800 per quality-adjusted life year gained. Our analysis accounts for healthcare system capacity constraints and equity considerations in intervention prioritization.
10.18632/aging.206330: This review synthesizes recent advances in AI-driven aging research, covering biomarker discovery, drug repurposing, and longevity intervention design. We examine how machine learning approaches have accelerated the identification of aging-related targets and the development of personalized anti-aging strategies. The review highlights the integration of multi-omics data with deep learning models for biological age prediction and intervention optimization.
10.48550/arXiv.2604.18539: We investigate emergent reasoning capabilities in graph neural networks through GraphReason, a framework that systematically evaluates logical inference on graph-structured data. Our experiments across knowledge graphs, molecular structures, and social networks reveal that attention-based GNNs develop abstract reasoning patterns through sufficient depth, achieving 78% accuracy on multi-hop reasoning tasks compared to 45% for shallow architectures.
10.48550/arXiv.2604.18535: We present MINT, a framework for mathematical inference augmented with tool use. MINT combines language model reasoning with symbolic computation, enabling complex mathematical derivations that require both pattern recognition and precise calculation. Evaluated on university-level mathematics problems, MINT achieves 67% accuracy compared to 38% for pure language model approaches, with particularly strong gains in calculus and linear algebra.
10.48550/arXiv.2604.18531: We introduce SynTask, a synthetic task generation framework for evaluating large language models. SynTask generates diverse, controllable evaluation tasks by composing atomic skill requirements into complex multi-step problems. The framework enables fine-grained capability assessment across reasoning, knowledge retrieval, and code generation, identifying specific failure modes that aggregate benchmarks obscure.
10.48550/arXiv.2604.18527: We investigate deductive closure in large language models, examining whether models that can individually prove p and q can also prove p∧q. Our systematic evaluation across propositional, first-order, and modal logic reveals that deductive closure is a persistent weakness, with closure accuracy 30-45% lower than individual proof accuracy. We propose chain-of-thought verification as a mitigation strategy.
10.48550/arXiv.2604.18523: We study test-time compute scaling in large language models, analyzing how allocating additional inference-time computation affects reasoning quality. Our experiments show that best-of-N sampling, chain-of-thought refinement, and iterative verification can improve task performance by 15-40% depending on problem difficulty. We derive scaling laws relating inference compute to accuracy across mathematical and coding benchmarks.
10.48550/arXiv.2604.18519: We investigate reward model ensembles for improving large language model alignment. Our ensemble approach combines multiple independently-trained reward models to produce more robust preference predictions. Experiments on helpfulness, harmlessness, and honesty benchmarks show that ensemble-based alignment reduces reward hacking by 35% compared to single-reward-model approaches while maintaining alignment quality.
10.48550/arXiv.2604.18515: We evaluate chain-of-thought prompting for scientific reasoning tasks across physics, chemistry, and biology domains. Our analysis reveals that structured CoT prompts with domain-specific reasoning templates improve scientific problem-solving accuracy by 22-31% over standard prompting. We identify that the primary benefit comes from decomposing complex scientific reasoning into verifiable intermediate steps.
10.48550/arXiv.2604.18511: We present a multimodal reasoning framework for medical diagnosis that integrates textual clinical notes, medical imaging, and laboratory data. Our approach uses a unified attention mechanism to perform cross-modal reasoning, achieving 84% diagnostic accuracy on complex cases compared to 71% for modality-specific models. The framework demonstrates particular strength in rare disease identification where multi-signal integration is essential.
